structure: California History-Social Science Framework (2016), K-12, organized by numbered chapters; running page headers 'Grade Eight'/'Grade Nine'/'Grade Ten'/'Grades Nine-Twelve' appear as text units at the top of each page (labeled backup). This part covers the end of Ch12 (Grade 8: units Envisioning a New America, Divergent Paths of the American People 1800-1850, Causes/Course/Consequences of the Civil War, Rise of Industrial America 1877-1914), Ch13 (Instructional Practice for Grades 9-12, backup), Ch14 (Grade 9 elective courses, each introduced by a course-title heading, a guiding question in 'n n' bullet lines, narrative, and Classroom Example boxes), and Ch15 (Grade 10 World History, Culture, and Geography: The Modern World, organized by unit headings with bulleted guiding questions, narrative, and Classroom Example boxes). Classroom Example boxes start with a heading 'Grade X Classroom Example: ...', continue after page breaks with 'Example (continued)', and end with an alignment line 'CA HSS Content Standard(s): ... CA HSS Analysis Skills ... CA CCSS ... CA ELD Standards ...'. No formal standards text (Appendix C) falls in this range; all chapter narrative, guiding questions, vignettes are 'examples'.
